name: Cortical Functional Localization and Aphasia Syndromes

reference.source: Clinical Neuroanatomy Made Ridiculously Simple / Brazis Localization
clinicalPearls: Broca area (Brodmann 44, 45) in dominant inferior frontal gyrus governs expressive motor speech programming
Broca aphasia: non-fluent, halting speech with intact comprehension and severe frustration
Wernicke area (Brodmann 22) in posterior superior temporal gyrus mediates receptive language comprehension
Wernicke aphasia: fluent effortless paraphasic speech with severely impaired comprehension and lack of insight
Arcuate fasciculus disruption causes conduction aphasia: fluent speech and intact comprehension, but severely impaired repetition
reference.pathophysiology: Cerebral cortex organization partitions executive, sensory, motor, and multimodal association tasks into discrete cytoarchitectonic Brodmann areas. Language networks link temporal auditory comprehension centers to frontal motor speech areas via the arcuate fasciculus. Ischemic destruction of these hubs or tracts produces specific language dissociations.
additionalInvestigations: Standardized bedside language evaluation (fluency, comprehension, repetition, naming)
